102: # 476 -- Placeholder token warning while Draft
103: 
104: ## 1. OVERVIEW
105: 
106: This scenario validates the Draft half of the versioned placeholder gate. A packet scaffolded from a v2.3 template carries `[YOUR_VALUE_HERE: ...]` tokens and a Status row that reads Draft. The gate must report an unfilled token as a warning and must not fail the strict run, because a planning commit is expected to hold tokens.
107: 
108: ### Why This Matters
109: 
110: A gate that fails a fresh scaffold blocks every new packet before its first word is written. A gate that passes a finished packet lets a weak model ship a document that still says `[YOUR_VALUE_HERE: feature name]`. This scenario proves the first half. Draft warns and passes.
111: 
112: ---

115:

119: - Playbook ID: 476.
120: - Real user request: `Scaffold a Level 2 packet, leave the value tokens unfilled, and tell me whether strict validation still passes while the packet is a Draft.`

1112: # Versioned placeholder gate
1113: 
1114: ## 1. OVERVIEW
1115: 
1116: The versioned placeholder gate decides the severity of an unfilled authoring token from the template stamp a document carries. A document stamped v2.3 or later warns while the packet status is Draft and fails at any other status. A document with an older stamp, or with no stamp, keeps the error it always had.
1117: 
1118: The gate exists so a planning commit can land with tokens still in place, while a finished packet cannot. It also keeps every existing packet on its old verdict, because a new rule that failed them would break an external repository on update.
1119: 
1120: ---
1121: 
1122: ## 2. HOW IT WORKS
1123: 
1124: ### Stamp Detection
1125: 
1126: The rule reads the first 70 lines of each document for a `SPECKIT_TEMPLATE_SOURCE` line. A version of v2.3 or later opens the gate. A version of v2.2 or earlier, or no line at all, leaves the document on the old rule.
1127: 
1128: ### Draft Lifecycle
1129: 
1130: When the gate is open, the rule reads the first Status row of the packet's `spec.md`. The exact word Draft, ignoring case, bold marks, backticks, quotes and trailing punctuation, makes an unfilled token a warning. Every other value, and a missing Status row, makes it an error. An open question marker is an error in both cases.
1131: 
1132: A warning does not fail `--strict`. The run passes when no other rule reports an error.
1133: 
1134: ### Scope
1135: 
1136: The orchestrator reads every authored document that is present. The shell mirror reads `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md` and `decision-record.md`, and it adds `acceptance-criteria.md`, `implementation-summary.md` and `goal.md` only when they carry the stamp. Both implementations answer with the same verdict, and one test file compares them.
1137: 
1138: ### Edge Cases
1139: 
1140: A fenced code block is skipped, so a token shown in an example does not fail a document. A token inside an inline code span is skipped for the same reason. A status such as `Draft (phase 3)` is not the word Draft, so it counts as any other value.

1112: # Versioned placeholder gate
1113: 
1114: ## 1. OVERVIEW
1115: 
1116: The versioned placeholder gate decides the severity of an unfilled authoring token from the template stamp a document carries. A document stamped v2.3 or later warns while the packet status is Draft and fails at any other status. A document with an older stamp, or with no stamp, keeps the error it always had.
1117: 
1118: The gate exists so a planning commit can land with tokens still in place, while a finished packet cannot. It also keeps every existing packet on its old verdict, because a new rule that failed them would break an external repository on update.
1119: 
1120: ---
1121: 
1122: ## 2. HOW IT WORKS
1123: 
1124: ### Stamp Detection
1125: 
1126: The rule reads the first 70 lines of each document for a `SPECKIT_TEMPLATE_SOURCE` line. A version of v2.3 or later opens the gate. A version of v2.2 or earlier, or no line at all, leaves the document on the old rule.
1127: 
1128: ### Draft Lifecycle
1129: 
1130: When the gate is open, the rule reads the first Status row of the packet's `spec.md`. The exact word Draft, ignoring case, bold marks, backticks, quotes and trailing punctuation, makes an unfilled token a warning. Every other value, and a missing Status row, makes it an error. An open question marker is an error in both cases.
1131: 
1132: A warning does not fail `--strict`. The run passes when no other rule reports an error.
1133: 
1134: ### Scope
1135: 
1136: The orchestrator reads every authored document that is present. The shell mirror reads `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md` and `decision-record.md`, and it adds `acceptance-criteria.md`, `implementation-summary.md` and `goal.md` only when they carry the stamp. Both implementations answer with the same verdict, and one test file compares them.
1137: 
1138: ### Edge Cases
1139: 
1140: A fenced code block is skipped, so a token shown in an example does not fail a document. A token inside an inline code span is skipped for the same reason. A status such as `Draft (phase 3)` is not the word Draft, so it counts as any other value.

1264: # Example drift guard
1265: 
1266: ## 1. OVERVIEW
1267: 
1268: The example drift guard is a read-only script that compares the hand-written example packets with the templates they came from. A model copies an example, so a drifted example teaches the model a structure the validator no longer expects.
1269: 
1270: The guard reports one line per problem and exits 1 on any drift. It exits 0 and prints `EXAMPLE_DRIFT_OK` when every example agrees with its template.
1271: 
1272: ---
1273: 
1274: ## 2. HOW IT WORKS
1275: 
1276: ### Anchor Comparison
1277: 
1278: The guard calls `runtime/cli/utils/template-structure.js compare <level> <doc> <example> anchors`. It fails on every `missing_anchor` line and every `extra_anchor` line. The compare step reads the level contract, so the guard inherits the required and optional anchor lists instead of hard-coding a copy.
1279: 
1280: ### Description Check
1281: 
1282: The guard reads the first `description:` line of each example. It fails when the line holds the end of an HTML comment, starts lowercase, or lacks a closing period. Those three defects were the leaked line phase 2 repaired, and the check keeps them from coming back.
1283: 
1284: ### Invocation
1285: 
1286: The script takes one optional directory. With no argument it reads `templates/examples`. With an argument it reads that directory, which lets a test run it against a scratch copy. A vitest wrapper runs it in the suite.

1333: # Spec authoring card
1334: 
1335: ## 1. OVERVIEW
1336: 
1337: The spec authoring card is the short authoring path for a model. It lives at `references/workflows/spec-authoring-card.md` and fits in one read. The `PLAN`, `IMPLEMENT`, `INTAKE` and `TEMPLATE_AUTHORING` intents load the card. The long template guide stays reachable from the on demand list only.
1338: 
1339: The card covers the bounds of a packet write, the level choice, the scaffold command, the fill rules, the validation command and the close steps. Each step carries one action, one acceptance line and one command.

1343: ## 2. HOW IT WORKS
1344: 
1345: ### Router Change
1346: 
1347: `RESOURCE_MAP` in `SKILL.md` lists the resources each intent loads. Four rows changed from the long guide to the card. The `ON_DEMAND` list keeps one guide entry, so a reader can still ask for the long path.
1348: 
1349: ### Sync Guard
1350: 
1351: `runtime/cli/spec/check-card-sync.sh` reads the card, the router, the generated leaf inventory files and the authoring checklist. 1352: 
1353: ### Inventory Regeneration
1354: 
1355: The card is a leaf resource, so the two generated inventory files list it. Both files are written by their generator scripts and are never edited by hand. The sync guard reads them, and the leaf inventory check reports a missing card entry.
1356: 
1357: ### Authoring Use
1358: 
1359: A model reads the card, scaffolds with `create.sh`, fills every section, removes every token, and runs `validate.sh --strict`. Three smoke runs measure the path, and the manual playbook holds a full end to end scenario.

1264: # Example drift guard
1265: 
1266: ## 1. OVERVIEW
1267: 
1268: The example drift guard is a read-only script that compares the hand-written example packets with the templates they came from. A model copies an example, so a drifted example teaches the model a structure the validator no longer expects.
1269: 
1270: The guard reports one line per problem and exits 1 on any drift. It exits 0 and prints `EXAMPLE_DRIFT_OK` when every example agrees with its template.
1271: 
1272: ---
1273: 
1274: ## 2. HOW IT WORKS
1275: 
1276: ### Anchor Comparison
1277: 
1278: The guard calls `runtime/cli/utils/template-structure.js compare <level> <doc> <example> anchors`. It fails on every `missing_anchor` line and every `extra_anchor` line. The compare step reads the level contract, so the guard inherits the required and optional anchor lists instead of hard-coding a copy.
1279: 
1280: ### Description Check
1281: 
1282: The guard reads the first `description:` line of each example. It fails when the line holds the end of an HTML comment, starts lowercase, or lacks a closing period. Those three defects were the leaked line phase 2 repaired, and the check keeps them from coming back.
1283: 
1284: ### Invocation
1285: 
1286: The script takes one optional directory. With no argument it reads `templates/examples`. With an argument it reads that directory, which lets a test run it against a scratch copy. A vitest wrapper runs it in the suite.

1954: | TASK-VERIFY | The conductor runs the task's verify command and reads both its output and its exit status before marking the task `[x]` |

1979:

1981:   <the paths this task names>
1982:

Usage: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/create.sh [options] <feature_description>

Creates a new spec folder with templates based on documentation level.

Options:
  --json              Output in JSON format
  --level N           Documentation level: 1, 2, 3, or 3+ (extended)
                      1=baseline, 2=verification, 3=full, 3+=extended
                      Default: 1
                      Creates spec-sections/ with modular documentation
  --with-lazy-addons  Add before-after.md, timeline.md, roadmap.md, and decision-record.md
                      (off by default; all are valid at every level)
  --with-goal         Add goal.md, the durable directive an operator sets as the session objective
                      (off by default; valid at every level. With --phase it writes child goals only,
                      and --level phase-parent writes a parent goal. Author or amend goals with /create:goal)
  --subfolder <path>  Create versioned sub-folder in existing spec folder
                      Auto-increments version (001, 002, etc.)
  --topic <name>      Topic name for sub-folder (used with --subfolder)
                      If not provided, uses feature_description
  --phase             Create phased spec (parent + child folders)
                      Mutually exclusive with --subfolder
  --phases <N>        Number of initial child phases (default: 3)
  --phase-names <list>  Comma-separated names for child phases
  --parent <path>     Add phases to existing parent spec folder (with --phase)
  --phase-parent <path>  Alias for --parent in phase mode (supports nested specs/ paths)
                      Bind a new phase's goal with /create:goal <parent> phase-add
                      Example: --phase-names "foundation,implementation,integration"
  --short-name <name> Provide a custom short name (2-4 words) for the branch
  --number N          Specify branch number manually (overrides auto-detection)
  --skip-branch       Create spec folder only, don't create git branch
  --path <dir>        Create the spec folder at this exact repo-relative path (implies --skip-branch)
  --help, -h          Show this help message

Documentation Levels (CORE + ADDENDUM architecture v2.0):

  Level 1 (Core ~270 LOC):     Essential what/why/how
    Files: spec.md, plan.md, tasks.md
    Lifecycle: implementation-summary.md after implementation starts

  Level 2 (Core + Verify):     +Quality gates, verification
    Adds: verification/testing sections in tasks.md, NFRs, edge cases, effort estimation

  Level 3 (Core + Verify + Arch): +Architecture guidance
    Adds: executive summary, risk matrix, ADR guidance

  Level 3+ (All addendums):    +Enterprise governance
    Adds: approval workflow, compliance, stakeholder matrix, AI protocols

Template Composition:
  Core templates (~270 LOC) are shared across all levels.
  Higher levels ADD value, not just length.
  Templates located in: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/

All levels include: scratch/ (working files; NOT git-ignored, add a scratch/.gitignore for anything you do not want committed)

Examples:
  .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/create.sh 'Add user authentication system' --short-name 'user-auth'
  .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/create.sh 'Implement complex OAuth2 flow' --level 2
  .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/create.sh 'Major architecture redesign' --level 3 --number 50

validate.sh - Spec Folder Validation (v3.0.0)

USAGE: ./validate.sh <folder-path> [OPTIONS]

OPTIONS:
    --help, -h     Show help     --version, -v  Show version
    --json         JSON output   --strict       Run strict-only rules
    --verbose      Detailed      --quiet, -q    Results only
    --recursive    Validate parent + all [0-9][0-9][0-9]-*/ child phase folders
    --no-recursive Disable auto-recursive validation when phase children exist

ENVIRONMENT:
    SPECKIT_RULES              Comma-separated subset of rules to evaluate
    SPECKIT_SKIP_VALIDATION    1, true, yes or on skips validation (also read from hook-flags.env)
    SPECKIT_STRICT/_VERBOSE/_JSON/_QUIET   Equivalent to the flags above

EXIT CODES: 0=pass, 1=user error, 2=validation error, 3=system error

RULES BY CATEGORY:
  authored_template:
    FILE_EXISTS [error] - Validates required spec documents for the declared documentation level.
    PLACEHOLDER_FILLED [error] - Rejects unfilled template placeholders in authored spec documents.
    COMMENT_HYGIENE_MARKER [error] - Rejects ephemeral finding markers inside HTML comments in authored spec documents.
    SCAFFOLD_NEVER_TOUCHED [error] - Rejects scaffold-signature markers in required docs when spec.md claims Complete status.
    STATUS_CROSS_DOC_CONSISTENCY [error] - Advisory-by-default check that spec.md and implementation-summary.md status fields classify to the same delivery state.
    LEVEL_DECLARED [info] - Reports whether the documentation level was declared or inferred.
    AC_COVERAGE [info] - Default-on advisory (non-blocking) scan for acceptance-criteria traceability coverage; set SPECKIT_AC_COVERAGE=false to opt out.
    AC_CLOSURE [error] - Gates packet closure on acceptance-criteria.md at Levels 2, 3 and 3+; unmet criteria block a completion claim and a waiver must cite an ADR that exists. Packets created before the cutoff stay advisory.
    ANCHORS_VALID [error] - Checks anchors in each spec doc whose template defines them, ignoring fenced code; a phase parent is exempt, and research/research.md and review/review-report.md are skipped as free-form workflow documents. Errors: a doc with no anchors, an anchor opened twice, never closed, closed but never opened, or closed more times than it is opened. Nesting is also an error: an anchor opened inside another, closed before it is opened, or closed while another is still open, though markers quoted in inline code are ignored by the nesting check; an adr-NNN anchor may hold adr-NNN-* anchors. Template order is not checked.
    FRONTMATTER_MEMORY_BLOCK [error] - Validates canonical _memory continuity frontmatter blocks.
    SPEC_DOC_SUFFICIENCY [error] - Checks implementation-summary sufficiency after save/write flows.
    TOC_POLICY [error] - Enforces table-of-contents placement policy.
    AI_PROTOCOLS [error] - Validates AI execution protocol sections in high-governance specs.
    COMPLEXITY_MATCH [error] - Checks declared level against content complexity signals.
    FOLDER_NAMING [error] - Validates numbered spec-folder naming conventions.
    FRONTMATTER_VALID [error] - Validates YAML frontmatter structure and required semantic values.
    FRONTMATTER_VALUES [warn] - Warns when a packet document's contextType or importance_tier is outside the shared list in sk-doc/sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-values.json. Aliases are legal.
    SOURCE_TAGS [warn] - Warns when a path:line citation inside a [SOURCE: ...] tag in a packet's research or review artifacts names a gone file, a moved file or a line past the end, using sk-doc's citation resolver. Packets created on or before the cutoff are skipped. A pass means the path and line exist, not that they support the claim.
    GREP_CONVENTION [error] - Checks every markdown document in a spec folder against the greppable-corpus convention: frontmatter variant, trigger phrase quality, anchor grammar and naming.
    LEVEL_MATCH [error] - Checks required files match the declared documentation level.
    SPEC_DOC_INTEGRITY [error] - Verifies inline markdown references resolve within spec docs.
    TEMPLATE_SOURCE [error] - Checks SPECKIT_TEMPLATE_SOURCE provenance markers.
  operational_runtime:
    MERGE_LEGALITY [error] - Validates generated merge payloads against target anchor shape.
    CROSS_ANCHOR_CONTAMINATION [error] - Detects route/category mismatches before generated content is merged.
    POST_SAVE_FINGERPRINT [error] - Verifies post-save fingerprints for generated writes.
    GRAPH_METADATA_PRESENT [warn] - Checks generated description and graph metadata are present.
    GRAPH_METADATA_CHILD_DRIFT [warn] - Flags graph-metadata.json children_ids missing on-disk phase children the writer would add (advisory unless SPECKIT_CHILD_DRIFT_ENFORCE=true).
    NORMALIZER_LINT [error] - Strict-only lint for duplicated runtime normalizer helpers.
    CANONICAL_SAVE_ROOT_SPEC_REQUIRED [error] - Ensures canonical saves include a root spec reference.
    CANONICAL_SAVE_SOURCE_DOCS_REQUIRED [error] - Ensures canonical saves include source document references.
    CANONICAL_SAVE_LINEAGE_REQUIRED [error] - Ensures canonical save lineage metadata is present.
    CANONICAL_SAVE_PACKET_IDENTITY_NORMALIZED [error] - Checks canonical save packet identity normalization.
    CANONICAL_SAVE_DESCRIPTION_GRAPH_FRESHNESS [error] - Checks generated description/graph freshness for canonical saves.
    CONTINUITY_FRESHNESS [error strict-only] - Strict-mode freshness check for continuity frontmatter. The rule reports warn by default and escalates to fail under SPECKIT_COMPLETION_FRESHNESS_ENFORCE; the ceiling here has to allow that escalation, since a warn ceiling would silently cap it.
    LINKS_VALID [warn] - Scans the system-spec-kit skill's own markdown for wikilinks whose target file does not exist. The target is always this skill, never the validated packet.
  structural:
    GRAPH_METADATA_CHILD_IDENTITY [error] - Flags graph-metadata.json children_ids entries whose leading path identity is not the packet's own current identity (stale rename residue the refresh writer now prunes).
    GRAPH_METADATA_SHAPE [warn] - Validates graph-metadata.json shape: required packet/derived blocks, last_active_child_id pointer integrity for phase parents.
    METADATA_DISK_PATH_CONSISTENCY [error] - Advisory-by-default check that description.json, graph-metadata.json, and continuity ids match the real on-disk spec-folder path.

Nesting is also an error: an anchor opened inside another, closed before it is opened, or closed while another is still open, though markers quoted in inline code are ignored by the nesting check; an adr-NNN anchor may hold adr-NNN-* anchors. Template order is not checked.
    FRONTMATTER_MEMORY_BLOCK [error] - Validates canonical _memory continuity frontmatter blocks.
    SPEC_DOC_SUFFICIENCY [error] - Checks implementation-summary sufficiency after save/write flows.
    TOC_POLICY [error] - Enforces table-of-contents placement policy.
    AI_PROTOCOLS [error] - Validates AI execution protocol sections in high-governance specs.
    COMPLEXITY_MATCH [error] - Checks declared level against content complexity signals.
    FOLDER_NAMING [error] - Validates numbered spec-folder naming conventions.
    FRONTMATTER_VALID [error] - Validates YAML frontmatter structure and required semantic values.
    FRONTMATTER_VALUES [warn] - Warns when a packet document's contextType or importance_tier is outside the shared list in sk-doc/sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-values.json. Aliases are legal.
    SOURCE_TAGS [warn] - Warns when a path:line citation inside a [SOURCE: ...] tag in a packet's research or review artifacts names a gone file, a moved file or a line past the end, using sk-doc's citation resolver. Packets created on or before the cutoff are skipped. A pass means the path and line exist, not that they support the claim.
    GREP_CONVENTION [error] - Checks every markdown document in a spec folder against the greppable-corpus convention: frontmatter variant, trigger phrase quality, anchor grammar and naming.
    LEVEL_MATCH [error] - Checks required files match the declared documentation level.
    SPEC_DOC_INTEGRITY [error] - Verifies inline markdown references resolve within spec docs.
    TEMPLATE_SOURCE [error] - Checks SPECKIT_TEMPLATE_SOURCE provenance markers.
  operational_runtime:
    MERGE_LEGALITY [error] - Validates generated merge payloads against target anchor shape.
    CROSS_ANCHOR_CONTAMINATION [error] - Detects route/category mismatches before generated content is merged.
    POST_SAVE_FINGERPRINT [error] - Verifies post-save fingerprints for generated writes.
    GRAPH_METADATA_PRESENT [warn] - Checks generated description and graph metadata are present.
    GRAPH_METADATA_CHILD_DRIFT [warn] - Flags graph-metadata.json children_ids missing on-disk phase children the writer would add (advisory unless SPECKIT_CHILD_DRIFT_ENFORCE=true).
    NORMALIZER_LINT [error] - Strict-only lint for duplicated runtime normalizer helpers.
    CANONICAL_SAVE_ROOT_SPEC_REQUIRED [error] - Ensures canonical saves include a root spec reference.
    CANONICAL_SAVE_SOURCE_DOCS_REQUIRED [error] - Ensures canonical saves include source document references.
    CANONICAL_SAVE_LINEAGE_REQUIRED [error] - Ensures canonical save lineage metadata is present.
    CANONICAL_SAVE_PACKET_IDENTITY_NORMALIZED [error] - Checks canonical save packet identity normalization.
    CANONICAL_SAVE_DESCRIPTION_GRAPH_FRESHNESS [error] - Checks generated description/graph freshness for canonical saves.
    CONTINUITY_FRESHNESS [error strict-only] - Strict-mode freshness check for continuity frontmatter. The rule reports warn by default and escalates to fail under SPECKIT_COMPLETION_FRESHNESS_ENFORCE; the ceiling here has to allow that escalation, since a warn ceiling would silently cap it.
    LINKS_VALID [warn] - Scans the system-spec-kit skill's own markdown for wikilinks whose target file does not exist. The target is always this skill, never the validated packet.
  structural:
    GRAPH_METADATA_CHILD_IDENTITY [error] - Flags graph-metadata.json children_ids entries whose leading path identity is not the packet's own current identity (stale rename residue the refresh writer now prunes).
    GRAPH_METADATA_SHAPE [warn] - Validates graph-metadata.json shape: required packet/derived blocks, last_active_child_id pointer integrity for phase parents.
    METADATA_DISK_PATH_CONSISTENCY [error] - Advisory-by-default check that description.json, graph-metadata.json, and continuity ids match the real on-disk spec-folder path.

# Manual Testing Playbook Snippet Template

Per-feature scenario files for split manual testing playbooks. Use this template for the one-file-per-feature contract described in the main playbook template.

> **EXECUTION POLICY**: Every scenario MUST be executed for real, never mocked or stubbed. AI agents executing these scenarios must run the actual commands, inspect real files, call real handlers, and verify real outputs. The only acceptable classifications are PASS, FAIL, or SKIP with a specific sandbox or runtime blocker documented.

<!-- MANUAL_PLAYBOOK_RESULT_PERSISTENCE_CONTRACT -->
> **COMPLETION**: This feature run is incomplete until its `PASS`, `FAIL`, or `SKIP` outcome and reason are recorded into `<skill>/benchmark/reports/<dated-run-label>/`. Generated report Markdown is renderer-owned.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

Each feature file is the canonical home for full scenario execution detail. The root `manual-testing-playbook.md` stays readable by summarizing the feature and linking here, while the feature file carries the realistic user-testing context, orchestration process, 9-column test row, structured source references, and concise metadata. The file shape should intentionally mirror the Feature Catalog snippet pattern so operators can move between the catalog and the playbook without relearning the document structure.

**Required uses**:
- One file per feature ID
- One primary 9-column scenario row per file
- Frontmatter that mirrors the larger root docs (`title` + `description`)
- Root playbook summary plus per-feature file cross-link
- Realistic user request and orchestrator prompt
- Desired user-visible outcome and execution process notes

**Do not use this template for**:
- General reusable prose fragments
- Replacing root-level review/release-readiness or orchestration guidance
- Spreading one feature across multiple primary files without a clear reason

**Validator note**: `scripts/validate-playbook-package.cjs` recurses into category folders and checks per-feature structure, required execution content, verdicts, local links, and root-index bijection. Cross-file markdown links are verified separately by the `check-markdown-links.cjs` CI guard.

---

## 2. TEMPLATE SCAFFOLD

Copy this into `manual-testing-playbook/{CATEGORY_DIR}/{FEATURE_SLUG}.md`. Both placeholder values must be kebab-case:

```markdown

title: "{FEATURE_ID} -- {FEATURE_NAME}"
description: "This scenario validates {FEATURE_NAME} for `{FEATURE_ID}`. It focuses on {OBJECTIVE}."
stage: routing   # routing | holdout | negative — benchmark-tier grouping; carries what a numbered filename prefix used to encode
# Routing-gold fields — REQUIRED when the scenario claims a route. Any one of them
# enrols the scenario in the topology gate (validate-playbook-topology.cjs), and
# validate-compiled-routing-scenarios.cjs rejects a compiled-routing scenario that
# lacks id, expected_intent or expected_resources. Omit them for a behavioural
# scenario that exercises a script or hook and makes no routing claim.
id: "{FEATURE_ID}"                       # stable scenario id; falls back to the filename if omitted
expected_intent: "{EXPECTED_INTENT}"     # routing intent/mode the skill should select for this prompt
expected_resources:                      # resource paths the correct route must load (one per line)
  - "{EXPECTED_RESOURCE_PATH}"
# Routing-gold topology fields — REQUIRED for a scenario that claims a route. The
# topology gate (validate-playbook-topology.cjs) resolves these against the hub's
# leaf-manifest.json, so omitting them fails the routing-gold contract even though
# the operator-scenario validator never checks them.
expected_workflow_mode: "{EXPECTED_WORKFLOW_MODE}"   # mode that owns the routed leaves
expected_leaf_resources:                             # one typed pair per leaf the route loads
  - workflow_mode: "{EXPECTED_WORKFLOW_MODE}"
    leaf_resource_id: "{LEAF_RESOURCE_ID}"
version: 1.0.0.0

- When a feature needs extra checks, add them beneath the main row instead of creating a second primary scenario row by default.

# Feature Catalog Snippet Template

Per-feature reference files for split feature catalogs. Use this template for the one-file-per-feature contract described in the main feature catalog template.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

Each feature file is the canonical home for detailed current-reality reference material. The root `feature-catalog.md` stays readable by summarizing the feature and linking here, while the per-feature file carries the fuller behavior description, structured source-file references, validation anchors, and concise metadata.

| Use this template when | Do NOT use this template for |
|---|---|
| Creating one file per catalog feature | General reusable prose fragments |
| Adding a feature to an existing split catalog | Replacing the root feature catalog |
| A feature needs structured source-file + test references | Splitting one feature across multiple files without clear reason |
| A feature maps to a named MCP tool or CLI command | Features not yet shipped (mark as not-yet-implemented in HOW IT WORKS instead) |

---

## 2. FRONTMATTER CONTRACT

All per-feature snippet files require this frontmatter block. Fields marked `# required` must appear in every file. Fields marked `# optional` may be omitted if not applicable.

```yaml
---
title: "{FEATURE_NAME}"                           # required — human-readable label, matches H3 in root catalog
description: "{ONE_LINE_FEATURE_SUMMARY}"         # required — shown in catalog tables and advisor doc matches
trigger_phrases:                                   # required — must match the H3 feature heading in the root catalog (doc-trigger harvest scans references/ and assets/, not feature-catalog/, so this list does not drive skill-advisor routing today)
  - "{primary trigger phrase}"
  - "{alternate phrasing}"
  - "{tool or command name}"
  - "{user-visible label if different}"
importance_tier: "important"                       # optional — omit unless this is a Tier 1 critical feature
version: 1.0.0.0
---
```

**Field notes:**
- `trigger_phrases` must match the H3 feature heading used in the root `feature-catalog.md` (plus natural language alternates)
- `importance_tier: "important"` is reserved for features that should rank as high-signal in skill-advisor routing. Omit it for standard entries
- `title` must equal the matching root H3 literally. `description` must match the root H3 Description after case, whitespace, and Markdown-punctuation normalization, so harmless punctuation differences are allowed, but a different claim is not.

---

## 3. TEMPLATE SCAFFOLD

Copy everything inside the code fence into `feature-catalog/{CATEGORY_DIR}/{FEATURE_SLUG}.md`. Both placeholder values must be kebab-case:

```markdown
---
title: "{FEATURE_NAME}"
description: "{OVERVIEW_ONE_LINE}"
trigger_phrases:
  - "{primary trigger phrase}"
  - "{alternate phrasing}"
  - "{tool or command name}"
  - "{user-visible label if different}"
# importance_tier: "important"   # uncomment only for Tier 1 critical features
version: 1.0.0.0
---

# {FEATURE_NAME} ({tool_name_or_command})

## 1. OVERVIEW

{OVERVIEW_ONE_LINE}

{OVERVIEW_DETAIL}

---

# System Spec Kit

> Every file change gets a documented why. Every new session picks up where the last one ended.

---

## 1. AT A GLANCE

| Aspect | What you get |
|---|---|
| **Use it for** | Capturing why code changed and resuming that reasoning across sessions |
| **Invoke with** | "spec kit", "spec folder", "memory save", "/speckit:resume" or automatic Gate 3 routing |
| **Works on** | File-modifying AI conversations that need a documentation trail and cross-session continuity |
| **Produces** | Templated spec folders at four levels, a validated file structure and entries in the committed trigger index |

---

## 2. OVERVIEW

### Why This Skill Exists

AI conversations that modify files leave no reasoning trail. The session ends and the why behind every decision vanishes. A new session starts from a blank slate, so the architecture you explained on Monday is gone by Wednesday. Without enforced documentation and durable continuity, one session cannot build on another.

### What It Does

System Spec Kit captures every file-modifying conversation in a templated spec folder at one of four documentation levels matched to task complexity. Those decisions stay findable across sessions because they are committed files: a generated trigger index matches a prompt against author-declared phrases, and ripgrep finds anything else. `/speckit:resume` rebuilds the active context from packet-local sources. `/speckit:save` routes session updates into canonical documentation surfaces so the next session picks up where the last one stopped, on any model or tool.

### How This Compares

Manual documentation is ad hoc and inconsistent. Basic RAG offers vector similarity over a stateless index. System Spec Kit replaces both with templated folders at four levels, validated structure, and retrieval that reads the committed tree rather than a shadow copy of it. Context survives across sessions in the packet's own documents rather than in copy-pasted notes or a store that can drift from them. Nothing decays: a decision stays exactly as legible on its four-hundredth day as on its first, and a phrase nobody wrote is a clean no-hit rather than a confident wrong answer.

### Requirements

- Node.js 22.12 or newer (Node 24 for a full install)
- TypeScript 5.0 or newer

3:description: "A script converts the core template hints to value tokens, two validator implementations get a stamp-gated Draft lifecycle, and a failing-first test with mutation checks, a scaffold smoke test and before and after strict counts over every packet prove it."
32:A Python script rewrites each bare hint of five templates into `[YOUR_VALUE_HERE: <hint>]` and a second script stamps them v2.3. The orchestrator function `validatePlaceholders` and the shell rule `check-placeholders.sh` both learn one lifecycle: for a doc stamped v2.3 or later, an unfilled token warns while `spec.md` has the Status Draft and errors otherwise. The conductor writes the failing test first, makes it pass, breaks the code three ways to prove the test notices, then proves no existing packet changed verdict by validating every folder under `specs/` before and after.
59:A stamp-gated lifecycle. The template stamp says which contract a doc was written under. The validator keeps the old strict verdict for any doc without the new stamp and applies the Draft lifecycle only to docs that carry it.
67:- `create.sh` function `finalize_scaffold_templates` replaces `[NAME]`, `[YYYY-MM-DD]`, `[Feature Name]` and `[###-feature-name]` and strips ` [template:...]` with `perl`. Function `ensure_template_source_near_top` moves the stamp line below the frontmatter. The stamp text, including its version, comes from the template.
68:- `templates/spec-kit-docs.json` lists a version per template, and `runtime/cli/tests/template-version-parity.vitest.ts` fails when a manifest version differs from the template stamp.
83:**Counts the conversion must give.** Converted per file: `spec.md.tmpl` 96, `plan.md.tmpl` 90, `tasks.md.tmpl` 7, `implementation-summary.md.tmpl` 11, `acceptance-criteria.md.tmpl` 10, so 214 in all. The total hint count of each file does not change, because a token is itself a hint under this regex. The bare hints left are exactly the ones in `tasks.md` T011.
85:**Stamp.** The 7 stamp lines of those five templates change from `| v2.2 -->` to `| v2.3 -->`: 3 in `spec.md.tmpl` and 1 each in the other four. The five manifest entries change the same way.
87:**Gate stamp.** A doc carries the gate stamp when one of its first 70 lines matches `<!-- SPECKIT_TEMPLATE_SOURCE: <names> | vMAJOR.MINOR -->` with MAJOR above 2, or MAJOR 2 and MINOR 3 or more. A doc with an older stamp or none does not.

94:| Gate stamp | any other value or none | error | error | fails |
95:| No gate stamp | any value | error | error | fails, as before |
111:Templates are converted and stamped. A scaffold made from them carries tokens and the v2.3 stamp. The orchestrator reads the stamp and the spec status for each doc and returns pass, warn or error for `PLACEHOLDER_FILLED`. The test drives the orchestrator through `validate.sh` and the shell rule through `bash -c`, and compares them.
129:| `runtime/cli/tests/upgrade-legacy.vitest.ts` | Removes a plan stamp line spelled with v2.2 from a rendered template | update one line to v2.3 | `tasks.md` T013 fourth and fifth blocks |
133:| `runtime/cli/spec/check-template-staleness.sh` | Compares a packet stamp with the manifest | unchanged, it will report older packets as stale | `plan.md` ADR-005 |
141:- Same-class producers: every `.tmpl` with a bare hint was counted with `rg -c '\[[A-Za-z/][^]\[]{2,}\]' templates/core/*.tmpl templates/addons/*.tmpl templates/packet-types/*.tmpl`. Only the five named templates are in scope. The other addons and packet types keep bare hints and their v2.2 stamps.
143:- Matrix axes: stamp (gate, older) by status (Draft, other) by marker (token, open question) makes 8 cells. The new test pins four: gate with Draft and token warns, gate with another status and token errors, older with Draft and token errors, gate with Draft and open question errors. The other four are the old behavior, covered by the 8 existing isolated cases and the 3 edge cases of the harness.
144:- Algorithm invariant: a warning is produced only when the doc has the gate stamp and the Status is Draft and the line holds no open question. Every other path reaches `findings` as before.
164:| Mutation | Remove the stamp gate, remove the Draft check, remove the stamp gate in the shell rule: each must turn the test red | `mutate.py` in `tasks.md` T010 |
165:| Integration | Scaffold, validate, flip status, downgrade stamp | `create.sh` and `validate.sh` in `tasks.md` T014 |
246:- [ ] No feature flag applies, the new lifecycle is selected by the template stamp
322:| M3 | Templates done | 214 tokens, 7 stamps, snapshot regenerated, smoke test as expected | Mid phase |
406:### ADR-001: Reuse the existing token and gate by the template stamp
412:**Decision**: No new grammar. A doc stamped v2.3 or later gets the Draft lifecycle. Any other doc keeps its old verdict.
416:- A hand-written doc that copies a v2.3 stamp opts itself in. That is the intended meaning of the stamp.
420:- Gating by packet creation date: dates are fragile across copies and renames, and the stamp already travels with the doc.
472:**Context**: `template-version-parity.vitest.ts` forces the manifest version to equal the template stamp, so the manifest must say v2.3. `repo-era.mjs` marks a document `legacy` when its stamp differs from the manifest. Run against this repository with the two manifests, the report went from 16871 `new` and 2374 `legacy` markers to 1421 `new` and 17824 `legacy`. `/doctor:update check` treats a `legacy` count above zero as a pre-v4 signal, so a repo with none today would start showing it. The validator verdict for every packet is unchanged.
474:**Decision**: This phase does not edit `repo-era.mjs` or the doctor command. It records the measured counts and three options in `goal.md` section 4 and in the closing report: accept the flip, teach the era report that v2.2 is still a current stamp for old docs, or hold the manifest bump until the doctor signal is adjusted.
488:**Context**: `upgrade-level.sh` renders sections from the templates into an older doc and does not touch the doc's template stamp. After this phase those sections arrive as tokens inside a doc that still says v2.2, and a token in a v2.2 doc is an error. Before this phase the same upgrade inserted bare hints that validated clean.
493:- An operator who upgrades an old packet to a higher level must fill the new sections or set the stamp.
505:**Decision**: Both get the same lifecycle in this phase. The shell rule reads `acceptance-criteria.md`, `implementation-summary.md` and `goal.md` only when they carry the gate stamp, so older docs are scanned exactly as before. One test file runs both on the same folder and compares the result.

if (rows.length === 0) process.exit(0);
const lines = ["[speckit] Recent packets in " + specsLabel + ", last 14 days:"];
for (const row of rows.slice(0, 10)) lines.push("  " + row.name.replace(controlChars, "") + "  " + row.date + "  " + row.description);
lines.push("[speckit] If the new work is a different change to the same artifact as one of these, join or create a series parent instead of a new packet: references/structure/phase-definitions.md, section 2.");
process.stderr.write(lines.join("\n") + "\n");
' "$SPECS_DIR" "$specs_label" || return 0
}

# Extracted to avoid duplication between phase mode and normal mode.
# Sets: BRANCH_SUFFIX, BRANCH_NUMBER, FEATURE_NUM, BRANCH_NAME
# Creates git branch unless SKIP_BRANCH=true or no git.
resolve_branch_name() {
    list_recent_track_packets
    if [[ -n "$SHORT_NAME" ]]; then
        BRANCH_SUFFIX=$(slugify_token "$SHORT_NAME")
    else
        BRANCH_SUFFIX=$(generate_branch_name "$FEATURE_DESCRIPTION")
    fi

    if [[ -z "$BRANCH_NUMBER" ]]; then
        # Number after the highest packet folder in the root being written to,
        # whatever its name, so two packets in one root never share a number.
        local highest=0
        if [[ -d "$SPECS_DIR" ]]; then
            for dir in "$SPECS_DIR"/*; do
                [[ -d "$dir" ]] || continue
                local dirname
                dirname=$(basename "$dir")
                local number
                number=$(echo "$dirname" | grep -o '^[0-9]\+' || echo "0")
                number=$((10#$number))
                if [[ "$number" -gt "$highest" ]]; then highest=$number; fi
            done
        fi
        # Without a track, a packet's branch shares the root's numbering, so a
        # numbered branch counts too. A track numbers from its folder alone.
        if [[ "$HAS_GIT" = true && -z "$TRACK" ]]; then
            local branch_highest
            branch_highest=$(highest_branch_number)
            if [[ "$branch_highest" -gt "$highest" ]]; then highest=$branch_highest; fi
        fi
        BRANCH_NUMBER=$((highest + 1))
    fi

    FEATURE_NUM=$(printf "%03d" "$((10#$BRANCH_NUMBER))")
    BRANCH_NAME="${FEATURE_NUM}-${BRANCH_SUFFIX}"

    # GitHub enforces 244-byte branch name limit
    local max_branch_length=244
    if [[ ${#BRANCH_NAME} -gt $max_branch_length ]]; then
        local max_suffix_length=$((max_branch_length - 4))
